comments.author: MeasIIDX
comments.body: Very cool to see! How did you go about building it out?

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body:
I used cursor ide, and started off with just making a game where you fly around and it was supposed to a dog fighting game. I use procedural generation on regular (non-voxel) terrain. But then I randomly decided that it would be cool to have destructible terrain, so I added voxels.

I tried this open world game, then I tried to make a monster survival game, but none really worked and I just liked to fly around really low to the ground and crash into the creatures. I wanted to make an open world flight racing game with beautiful scenery, but the game was lagging so much (I'm new to game dev). So then I pivoted to underground tunnel racing and the speed improved because I could use less chunks at a time. 

Long story short I got this far with the tunnel racing game, but its really a hodge podge of all the previous tries rolled up into one, it needs a full rebuild but I'm not sure if its worth it at this point. Other projects ideas are getting my attention

comments.author: Commercial_Lawyer_33
comments.body: it looks fun dude just fix that lag

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body:
yea thats my main battle right now! I have no clue what to try next except make making the chunk streaming and meshing extremely precise. It takes about 300ms for a chunk to go from pure data to a visibly textured voxels and as you fly through and change camera angles it gets tricky because we both need the chunks ready before hand, but also we dont want to do too much and cause lag. 

Maybe I've gotta look into what parts of the pipeline are causing frames to stop because Id rather have a smooth 60 fps even if the terrain is transitioning from un-meshed to meshed..
